# List-limit test checks an undrained reply cache

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

The test intended to prove that session listings respect their concurrency limit can now pass even if a listing replies before a slot is available. Typing still exercises the connection reader, but the test no longer observes replies until after it frees the slot.

## Details

At handlers.rs:10669-10693 the replacement type_and_see_received writes a grid input frame and waits directly on TestHost::received_contains. Unlike the removed echo helper, it never calls read_one. Only read_one at 10600-10641 populates host.replies. In a_list_waiting_for_its_own_limit_does_not_hold_up_typing, the last read happens during BusyHost initialization, before request 3 is sent. Lines 11299-11308 then assert request 3 is absent from that unchanged cache, release all held list permits, and only afterward call reply(3). Therefore an implementation that answers a list immediately without acquiring list_admission passes the no-early-reply assertion and the eventual SessionList assertion. This is a source-established test-evidence gap, not a claim of an observed runtime defect. SPEC.md:4707-4736, Waiting between operations on one host, requires terminal and listing progress; this test additionally declares the list's own limit as its target contract at 11273-11289. Restore an ordered observation of the connection output while the permits remain held, so the negative assertion examines frames through the typing boundary.

# List-limit test checks an undrained reply cache

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

The test for the session-list concurrency limit cannot detect a reply arriving before a list slot becomes available. It checks a cached reply list without reading the connection after sending the request, then frees the slots before receiving the answer.

## Details

Synthesis confirmed the exact observation sequence. BusyHost::initialize at handlers.rs:10488-10551 reads the handshake, Attached and initial ReplayComplete before request 3 exists; it then saturates management slots. The list-limit test at 11287-11317 holds all list permits, sends request 3, waits for type_and_see_received, and examines host.replies. Between that send and the absence assertion there is no read_one, reply, concurrent fixture reader, or other operation that can populate the cache. send at 10595-10600 writes only; type_and_see_received at 10669-10695 writes input and directly awaits TestHost's received-byte watch. Only read_one at 10606-10641 adds to replies, and reply at 10646-10661 invokes that reader. The next call is reply(3) at 11311, after drop(held) at 11310.

The server-side connection reader processing the marker is not a client-output observation barrier. connection.rs:455-581 dispatches the marker through the attached terminal's input. Its writer is a separate task at 921-997 and may leave the list reply queued or already written into the duplex stream without the fixture reading it. Thus the absence assertion examines an unchanged cache even when request 3 has already answered. In the previous revision, handlers.rs:11196-11213 read client frames until the terminal echo arrived, collecting control frames encountered before that marker. That was not proof that every concurrently spawned list task had settled, but it did observe replies ahead of the marker in the output stream; this patch removes even that negative oracle.

This is specifically a test-evidence regression: handle_list_sessions at 585-615 still acquires list_admission inside its spawned task and releases it before sending the reply. No current semaphore-bypass runtime defect is alleged. SPEC.md:4707-4736 requires terminal and list progress while management is busy, and this test's explicit contract at handlers.rs:11275-11285 additionally says the list waits for its own limit. The test still detects awaiting the list permit inline on the connection reader, since that blocks the input marker. It loses detection of an early reply or skipped list semaphore. A fix needs an explicit connection-output observation before releasing permits, or a direct deterministic admission/worker-boundary oracle; the typing watch alone is insufficient.

Suggested bucket: other (test validity only). Confidence: confirmed by source and caller/data-flow analysis. could-be-highest: no established security or user-owned-work route. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; excluded metadata and queue were not read. No reproduction, test, or execution observation. Original consequence is retained and narrowed to the lost negative reply oracle; the former echo was never a universal scheduling barrier.

# Keep the target host alive through conformance observation

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

The contention test for terminal controls shuts down the terminal it means to exercise before sending the control. This can fail the test's live-terminal premise or leave it testing cleanup of a dead terminal instead of normal controls under load.

## Details

In declared_nonblocking_requests_process_the_following_frame_under_contention, the prepared async task creates (terminal, _target_host) at handlers.rs:10895-10902 and attaches that terminal to channel 2 at 10947-10973. # Keep the target host alive through conformance observation

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

The terminal-control contention test disposes of its target host before sending the control it is supposed to test. A still-running output task does not preserve the healthy target-terminal premise. The result can be a premise failure or an observation of a route whose host has already been torn down.

## Details

Synthesis traced ownership end to end. handlers.rs:10895-10901 binds the TestHost owner in the prepared async future, while only its HostTerminal is inserted into the session entry. adopt_test_host at hosts/terminal/test_host.rs:365-372 returns these as separate values; TestHost exclusively owns the host serve-task JoinHandle, child process, and temporary socket directory (78-108, 434-487). HostTerminal::Inner at hosts/terminal.rs:1232-1280 owns the supervisor client runtime and channels, not a TestHost or its serve-task/child ownership. Cloning the terminal into a session or attachment cannot retain the stand-in host. The preparation future returns only (message, listener) at handlers.rs:10982, so _target_host is dropped before that future completes and before its JoinHandle resolves at 10985. No successful preparation path for these cases carries the owner into the later observation.

TestHost::drop at test_host.rs:104-108 requests task abortion and calls kill_child. kill_child at 126-132 takes the child, calls kill and wait; dropping the remaining TestHost fields also removes its temporary socket directory. Task abort is a cancellation request, not synchronous proof that the serving future has already finished. Kill/wait errors are ignored. These caveats do not restore the fixture's ownership or healthy-live-host guarantee: cleanup has already been initiated, and under the fixture's normal successful child cleanup the target child is reaped before observation begins. This finding is the unconditional premature disposal, not a claim that every run reaches one particular asynchronous terminal state.

The selected controls are real channel-2 operations: request_modes.rs:305-310 declares Detach, Resize, PauseOutput and ResumeOutput as InlineControl, using the chosen context's channel/session. In handlers.rs:3049-3073 they dispatch to set_attachment_paused, handle_detach or handle_resize. Pause/resume mutate the matched attachment watch (connection.rs:1546-1558); Detach takes and joins its forwarder (handlers.rs:1981-2006); Resize resolves its terminal and issues resize if attachment ownership still matches (2019-2084). Thus the patch does not necessarily bypass every relevant handler when the host ends: a surviving attachment can still exercise its lock/map branch. The lost premise is that these actions act on the live target terminal required by the test's own setup comments and live-route check (10893-10894 and 11036-11058). That check tests !forwarder.is_finished(), not host ownership, child liveness or host-task availability. Grid output reacts separately to runtime status (grid_stream.rs:602-668), so a live forwarder can temporarily coexist with prior host disposal. Conversely, if teardown has propagated, the premise can fail. No failing or passing schedule was observed or reproduced. The independent BusyHost::agent_host remains correctly retained and proves only channel-1 typing; it cannot keep channel 2 alive.

Later revisions: all relevant path changes from this commit through pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db were inspected. The handler changes only remove grid/terminal-kind protocol fields; TestHost changes only module wording. At tip, the same owner remains local at handlers.rs:10855, the future returns (message, listener) at 10941, and the output-task check occurs later at 11002-11017. The lifetime defect is still present. Keep the owner in the outer fixture/prepared result through action and cleanup. This record is specific to this conformance fixture, not another fixture's guard or exit oracle.

Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test validity and possible failure). Confidence: confirmed source lifetime defect; runtime schedule outcome unobserved. could-be-highest: no established security or user-owned-work route. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; excluded metadata and queue not read. No tests, runtime probes, or reproductions. Original consequence retained with explicit distinction between disposing of the host and the later asynchronous output-task state.
